name: The Bonnacon

tenures.role: wrestler — a caged "legendary creature" gimmick, revealed and staged as a monster rather than billed as a man

notes: Revealed on the GENESIS card by the Local NVA Company (Duc Chu Song and Thai Trang), who wheel him out in a cage and stage him as a mythical, fire-breathing creature of "the darkest jungles of Southeast Asia" rather than as a wrestler with a name of his own — the gimmick's only line ("UUURRRPPPP!") is a belch, not dialogue. Named for the bonnacon of medieval bestiary tradition (a bull-like beast that repels pursuers with caustic excrement), restaged here as the Local NVA Company's own monster mascot. The orientalist framing of the reveal (the Local NVA Company's own "legendary creature" showmanship, tied to their own already-flagged caricature) is part of the same era-typical staging — see /curation.html — though the Bonnacon's own billed name carries no ethnic caricature of its own.
caption: A caged, fire-breathing "legendary creature" the Local NVA Company wheels out on the GENESIS card, its only line a belch.

name: Wendel Hyroniemus Osvaldo Allen
caption: An usher who lost his job, his wife and his last dollar in one day until a song made him WHOA: the character concept sent to the UiWF's staff on 13 February 2011.
notes: Known from one application to the UiWF dated 13 February 2011, served at /promotions/uiwf/archive/whoa-uiwf-application-2011-02-13.html: Wendel Allen loses his job as a movie-theatre usher, his marriage and his last dollar to a bowling-alley vending machine in one day, hears a song that alters his view of life and 'becomes the song': 'WHOA is my initials.' The form closes on the line 'or some lame concept like that...'. The thread holds no reply. Shares the word WHOA with the NAPW record Modo WHOA! (2007); nothing in either record joins them (#no-auto-merge-no-silent-distinctness).

identity.note: Shares only the word WHOA with the NAPW record Modo WHOA! (2007); no card, roster or text names both, so they are filed distinct.
